solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Give travel guidance the shortest way

definitions.meaning: to tell someone how to get somewhere, as a verb
going straight, by the most immediate route, as an adjective or adverb

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means pointing someone the way; as an adjective it means straight and without detours.

clue.text: She separated from Charles and upset Nadia

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman leaves her husband Charles and distresses her friend Nadia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges NADIA. The Princess of Wales separated from Prince Charles in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: The Princess of Wales famously separated from Prince Charles, so she is the woman described.

definitions.meaning: snubs or rejects curtly
buffs a second time, a prefix of repetition added to a word for polishing

explanation.definitionFit: A snub is a brush-off; read as two parts, the word is buffing again, polishing a second time.

parts.note: taken literally, eyes that both look inwards towards the nose, rather than meaning introspective

explanation.definitionFit: A squint with both eyes turned towards the nose is literally looking inward, a joke on introspection.

clue.text: Refuge a youth originally found in squat

indicators.note: found in means one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a squat is a run-down building occupied illegally, so a slum

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word youth

explanation.surface: A young person seeking shelter ends up in an illegally occupied house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts Y, the first letter of 'youth' ('originally'), inside SLUM, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge is a place of safety, and political asylum is a sanctuary granted by a state.

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a British prime minister; the possessive gives Peel's

explanation.surface: A former prime minister has gone upstairs for a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone up' reverses PEELS, Peel's, from Sir Robert Peel, a nineteenth-century British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Rest and slumber are near synonyms, both a period of repose.

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or open grassland, a poetic word

indicators.note: untidy means disordered, so the letters of the word left are scrambled

explanation.surface: A stretch of meadow has been left messy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' looks like a piece of land, which the grassland in the surface encourages, but it is a printed pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, typically religious or political, handed out as printed matter.

clue.text: Chap to leave a served vegetable

parts.note: to get out is to leave

explanation.surface: A man is told to go away from a vegetable that has been served up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a served' is link padding for the dish on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangetout is a variety of pea eaten whole, pod and all, a green vegetable.

clue.text: Sailor returns with broken booms, they're hollow-stemmed

indicators.note: returns means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the word booms are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor comes back to find the ship's booms broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns AB into BA, and 'broken' rearranges BOOMS into MBOOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo grasses have hollow woody canes, so these plants are hollow-stemmed.

clue.text: Doesn't let go — sets free instead

indicators.note: sets free means the letters of the word instead are released into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who refuses to release a prisoner and frees others in their place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets free' rearranges INSTEAD; the surface contrasts holding with freeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in custody or keep them back is to refuse to let them go.

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: insular means cut off, isolated like an island

explanation.surface: A writer in a battle area is nearly cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims INSULAR to INSULA. The Peninsular War (1807-14) was fought in Spain and Portugal against Napoleon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian peninsula was the theatre of the Peninsular War, so it was a war zone.

parts.note: off as in nodded off, asleep, and fifty per cent as half; not a sale discount

explanation.definitionFit: Dozing is being only partly off to sleep, so fifty per cent dropped off is drowsy.

definitions.meaning: is lying flat, face down
falsehoods, fibs

explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to be prone; and falsehoods told are fibs, the plural noun.

clue.text: Starting comedy university cast finds it easy

indicators.note: starting points to the first letter of the word comedy

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast

explanation.surface: A student comedy production finds the going easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting' takes C from 'comedy'. 'cast' looks like a set of actors but means throw, SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job is comfortable and undemanding, an easy number.

definitions.meaning: a winner, one who triumphs
William I of England, known by this title after 1066

explanation.definitionFit: A winner in battle is one who triumphs; William of Normandy won England in 1066 and took the title.

parts.note: in means during, as in in the night
action means fighting, as in killed in action

explanation.surface: A soldier takes a break in the middle of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' looks like the remainder, but it means idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness, doing nothing, is a state of rest from activity.

parts.note: not lost people sought by police, but those not present, such as pupils away from school

explanation.definitionFit: People who are away from work or school are missing in the plain sense of not being present.

indicators.note: out means put out of shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone meddles and gets thrown out for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like a phrase for being evicted; 'out' alone rearranges IS TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle or interfere is to butt in where one is not wanted.

definitions.meaning: to hold in high regard, as a verb
politeness and deference, as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: Esteem for someone is appreciating them, and showing deference is courtesy.

clue.text: Take vain steps to provide support

definitions.meaning: to walk proudly and pompously, as a verb
a bar or brace holding up a structure, as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: A vain person swaggers when walking, and a brace in a framework bears a load.

clue.text: Right to be overjoyed when told

explanation.surface: Someone is right to be delighted when they hear the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told' looks like part of the story but means recounted, as a story is related.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to recount or tell it, so a related story is one told.

clue.text: One assumes them to be failures

definitions.meaning: one puts on clothes, assumes as in dons; slang for clothes
things that do not work, flops

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for clothes, which one puts on; and flops or useless things that fail.

parts.note: a wrestling hold, and the word son is the second half of a famous admiral's surname

explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling hold applied under one arm; also the last three letters of the admiral's name are son.

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the word heart are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A jilted lover with a broken heart talks about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartbroken' is one word in the surface but splits into fodder 'Heart' and indicator 'broken'. 'converse' means opposite, not talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of one who loves is one who detests, so the converse of a lover.

clue.text: Where to keep one's hose readily available

definitions.meaning: attached to a faucet, ready for watering
ready for immediate use, like beer from the barrel

explanation.definitionFit: A garden hose is kept connected to the faucet; and something ready to draw on is easily available.

definitions.meaning: halts or stops something
apprehensions of suspects, which police make

explanation.definitionFit: To halt growth is to check it; and police detain suspects by taking them into custody.

parts.note: not procrastinating, but leaving things after one's death, being late, by a valid will

explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies having made a valid will leaves possessions as the late deceased.

clue.text: Go back — but not to work

definitions.meaning: withdraw or retreat
stop working for good at the end of a career

explanation.definitionFit: An army withdraws or falls back, and a worker leaves employment for good at the end of a career.

clue.text: Exhausted when given high level employment

definitions.meaning: completely spent, all gone
employed, with up as a high level, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: Resources completely spent are all consumed; read in parts, employed and raised high.
